fullPassage:
(A) While the cafeteria was full of high school students on that afternoon, Dave was thirsty. We sat near yet away from him, fixing our hair and worrying about the test next period we hadn't studied for. (a) He was far away from our world, yet forced to be a part of it.

(B) Although it was clear that they were from very different worlds, for one moment, they'd shared a real understanding. As I walked away from my lunch table that day, I looked at Dave. I thought he and the dollar were very much alike. They both weren't accepted where the world said they were supposed to be. But just as the dollar had found a place in a warm-hearted senior's pocket, I was sure (b) he would eventually find his, too.

(C) But for some reason, he decided against it. He wasn't leaving until he got a drink. With a determined expression, (c) he kept aimlessly pushing the dollar bill into the machine. Just then a popular senior boy stood up from his seat, and walked over to the boy. (d) He calmly explained how the machine often had trouble accepting dollar bills. After that, he pulled some coins from his pocket and put them into the machine. Dave gave him his dollar and chose a flavor of fruit juice. Then the two walked off in different directions.

(D) He stood at the drink machine with purpose, fumbling through his fake leather wallet for some change. He came up with a wrinkled dollar bill, and nervously glanced back at his table where other students in (e) his class were sitting. Dave tried to make the machine accept his money. After he failed a few times, some students began to laugh at him. He started shaking, and tears began to form in his eyes. I saw him turn to sit down, looking like he had given up.

questions.passage:
(A) While the cafeteria was full of high school students on that afternoon, Dave was thirsty. We sat near yet away from him, fixing our hair and worrying about the test next period we hadn't studied for. (a) He was far away from our world, yet forced to be a part of it.

(B) Although it was clear that they were from very different worlds, for one moment, they'd shared a real understanding. As I walked away from my lunch table that day, I looked at Dave. I thought he and the dollar were very much alike. They both weren't accepted where the world said they were supposed to be. But just as the dollar had found a place in a warm-hearted senior's pocket, I was sure (b) he would eventually find his, too.

(C) But for some reason, he decided against it. He wasn't leaving until he got a drink. With a determined expression, (c) he kept aimlessly pushing the dollar bill into the machine. Just then a popular senior boy stood up from his seat, and walked over to the boy. (d) He calmly explained how the machine often had trouble accepting dollar bills. After that, he pulled some coins from his pocket and put them into the machine. Dave gave him his dollar and chose a flavor of fruit juice. Then the two walked off in different directions.

(D) He stood at the drink machine with purpose, fumbling through his fake leather wallet for some change. He came up with a wrinkled dollar bill, and nervously glanced back at his table where other students in (e) his class were sitting. Dave tried to make the machine accept his money. After he failed a few times, some students began to laugh at him. He started shaking, and tears began to form in his eyes. I saw him turn to sit down, looking like he had given up.

det.korean: were → was (진짜 주어 the cafeteria가 단수라서 was)
det.analysis:
밑줄 친 ①이 있는 문장은 'While the cafeteria ①<u>were</u> full of high school students(그 카페테리아가 고등학생들로 가득 차 있는 동안)'예요.

이 문장의 주어는 'the cafeteria(그 카페테리아)' 하나예요. 바로 뒤에 복수 명사 'high school students'가 있어서 were로 쓰고 싶어지지만, 그 학생들은 주어가 아니라 '무엇으로 가득 찼는지(full of ~)'를 설명하는 부분일 뿐이에요.

진짜 주어 the cafeteria는 단수(하나)이고 지난 일을 이야기하는 과거 시제라, be동사는 복수형 were가 아니라 단수형 was를 써야 해요.

그래서 밑줄 친 were는 was로 고쳐야 맞아요.
det.tip: 'of ~' 같은 수식어구·옆의 복수 명사는 무시하고 진짜 주어(the cafeteria, 단수)에 동사를 맞춘다 → was

[조건] (1) accepting, bills, dollar, had, machine, often, the, trouble를 모두 사용할 것 (2) (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 정답: the machine often had trouble accepting dollar bills
det.analysis:
주어는 the machine(그 기계)이에요. 빈도부사 often은 일반동사 had 앞에 놓아 the machine often had 순서가 돼요.

'~하는 데 어려움을 겪다'는 have trouble + 동사-ing라서 had trouble accepting으로 연결해요.

무엇을 받아들이는지 dollar bills(지폐)를 맨 뒤 목적어로 붙여 완성해요.
det.tip: have trouble + 동사-ing = ~하는 데 어려움을 겪다 / 빈도부사(often)는 일반동사 앞

(A) While the cafeteria was full of high school students on that afternoon, Dave was thirsty. We sat near yet away from him, fixing our hair and worrying about the test next period we hadn't studied for. (a) He was far away from our world, yet forced to be a part of it.

(B) Although it was clear that they were from very different worlds, for one moment, they'd shared a real understanding. As I walked away from my lunch table that day, I looked at Dave. I thought he and the dollar were very much alike. They both weren't accepted where the world said they were supposed to be. But just as the dollar had found a place in a warm-hearted senior's pocket, I was sure (b) he would eventually find his, too.

(C) But for some reason, he decided against it. He wasn't leaving until he got a drink. With a determined expression, (c) he kept aimlessly pushing the dollar bill into the machine. Just then a popular senior boy stood up from his seat, and walked over to the boy. (d) He calmly explained how the machine often had trouble accepting dollar bills. After that, he pulled some coins from his pocket and put them into the machine. Dave gave him his dollar and chose a flavor of fruit juice. Then the two walked off in different directions.

(D) He stood at the drink machine with purpose, fumbling through his fake leather wallet for some change. __________, and nervously glanced back at his table where other students in (e) his class were sitting. Dave tried to make the machine accept his money. After he failed a few times, some students began to laugh at him. He started shaking, and tears began to form in his eyes. I saw him turn to sit down, looking like he had given up.

"그는 구겨진 1달러짜리 지폐를 꺼냈다."

[ a / bill / came / dollar / he / up / with / wrinkled ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: he came up with a wrinkled dollar bill
det.analysis:
우리말 '그는 구겨진 1달러짜리 지폐를 꺼냈다'를 영어 어순으로 배열하는 문제예요.

먼저 주어 '그는' he를 맨 앞에 놓아요.

'꺼냈다(찾아냈다)'는 세 단어가 한 덩어리인 'come up with(~을 찾아내다·꺼내다)'를 과거형으로 바꿔 'came up with'로 이어요 → he came up with.

무엇을 꺼냈죠? '구겨진 1달러짜리 지폐'예요. 명사 앞에 꾸미는 말을 차례로 붙여 a(하나의) → wrinkled(구겨진) → dollar(달러) → bill(지폐) 순서로 'a wrinkled dollar bill'을 만들어요.

전부 이으면 he came up with a wrinkled dollar bill, 총 8단어예요.
det.tip: come up with = ~을 찾아내다/꺼내다 (세 단어가 한 덩어리) / 꾸미는 말 순서 a → wrinkled → dollar → bill

다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.

나는 그가 앉으려고 몸을 돌리는 것을 보았다.
[조건] (1) down, him, I, saw, sit, to, turn를 모두 사용할 것 (2) (7단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 정답: I saw him turn to sit down
det.analysis:
'나는 ~을 보았다'가 뼈대라 I saw로 시작해요.

see는 지각동사라 'see + 목적어 + 동사원형' 형태예요. 그래서 him turn(그가 몸을 돌리는 것을)처럼 turn 앞에 to를 쓰지 않아요.

'앉으려고'라는 목적은 to sit(to부정사)으로 나타내고, down을 붙여 sit down(앉다)으로 완성해요.
det.tip: 지각동사 see + 목적어 + 동사원형(turn) / to sit = ~하려고(목적)
